strategies.name: liquidity_sweep_inversion_5m_1m

entry_sequence.action: Identify the draw on liquidity, which can be Asia high/low, London high/low, or previous day high/low, or equal highs/lows.
entry_sequence.rationale: The draw on liquidity is the most important thing to identify.

entry_sequence.action: After 9:30 AM NY time, wait for a 5-minute or 15-minute fair value gap (FVG) to form towards the identified draw on liquidity.
entry_sequence.rationale: The FVG acts as the higher timeframe IRL (Internal Range Liquidity).

entry_sequence.action: Wait for price to tap into the higher timeframe FVG (5m or 15m).
Drop down to the 1-minute timeframe and look for an inversion setup.
Ensure the 1-minute price has swept some liquidity before tapping into the higher timeframe FVG or 15-minute FVG.
entry_sequence.rationale: This is a liquidity sweep check.

entry_sequence.action: Wait for the 1-minute price to close below the FVG (for a bullish FVG) or above the FVG (for a bearish FVG), creating an inversion.
entry_sequence.rationale: Inversion is when price disrespect[s] the FVG and closes on the opposite side, turning the FVG into resistance/support.

entry_sequence.action: Take a short position immediately after the 1-minute price closes below the bullish FVG.
entry_sequence.rationale: The inversion makes the FVG a resistance for price.

entry_sequence.action: Take a long position immediately after the 1-minute price closes above the bearish FVG.
entry_sequence.rationale: The inversion makes the FVG a support for price.

stop.rationale: Stop is placed above the high of the 1-minute candle that created the inversion.

strategies.stop_management: Go break even as soon as the closest liquidity after your entry is taken out.

targets.rationale: The speaker suggests going for a fixed 1:2 risk-to-reward ratio.
